customize.text: Aila

After the Golden City of Hyperborea fell six thousand years ago, its descendants, known as the Frostmoon Scions, began to govern the proliferation of countless subsequent generations by law. This was to continue until the blood, thinned by disaster and exile, was purified into holy seed, and mortal descendants were born as perfect beings, fully one with the world. But when, hundreds of generations later, the girl chosen to bear the sacred heir abandoned her mission for a young officer from Snezhnaya and slit her own throat for her love, her death precipitated the fulfillment of the prophecy, and her child never became the chosen one who would lead the Frostmoon Scions to Elysium. The Archpriestess, Lovia, was unwilling to wait hundreds of years for another child of sufficient purity to be born, so she turned to a lesser branch of the bloodline. The twin sisters born into this lineage were pale shadows of the one they were meant to replace, so Lovia committed an act so profane that even the mistress of the Frost Moon would recoil in horror at the blasphemy. Lovia began feeding the sisters the blood of the Frostmoon Scions from childhood.

Sisters Aila and Alia were born imperfect, sharing a single breath. In the brief moments between agonies, moments that should have been filled with joy, they huddled together, drawing what little warmth they could from each other. They had never seen their parents, nor had they ever heard the wind whispering through the groves. The two of them had only their grandmother, and the only way they'd seen the world was through the pages of a faded storybook. The worn pages revealed a world they had never seen: a single white bird, a streak of grace, gliding beneath a perfect moon. As they admired the free creatures of the fairy tales, the two children made a promise to each other that one day, the two of them would fly together like the white birds in the vast sky. <color=#ffffffd9>"Since the day we were born, it's always been just the two of us. When the day comes for us to leave, let's live the rest of our lives together."</color> But Aila's older sister, Alia, did not keep her promise and set off alone on a long journey that turned out not to be a flight toward a brighter future, but a fall into a much darker night. When the blessed lady's child, Avrelian, returned to Nod-Krai, not becoming the chosen heir of the Frostmoon Scions, Alia fled with him, leaving Aila alone. When Alia ran away, half the dream and half the pain meant for them both vanished with her. From that day on, Aila began to experience twice the torment.

<color=#ffffffd9>"So you lied to me all along as well... My older sister, the only one I ever truly trusted."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"But I won't resent you... I have long lost hope for the sky beyond."</color>

From then on, all hope for the birth of the sacred heir fell on the younger sister, and she grew up under the control of the Archpriestess, never forgiving Avrelian. With unwavering faithfulness, Aila carried out every last one of the venerable Archpriestess's commands, no matter how dreadful the punishments cloaked by her soft words. Whether someone's thread was to be severed by a sharp silver blade, or another's singing voice must be silenced in the dead of night, all sins were borne to purify the holy blood bestowed by the moon, for only by drinking crimson water could one hone absolute flawlessness.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Here, drink this pure moonlight, my beloved child, my most cherished child!"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Let it weave into your flesh and blood, so that you too may be worthy of the gods' grace."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Look to the apostle of the Golden City. How he drank bitter wine and fought for the freedom of his compatriots!"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Like him, you must embrace this joyous pain, for from it, perfection will one day be born."</color>

customize.text: Lovia's Death

More than five hundred years ago, the Archpriestess Lovia allied with the monk Rotwang, who had arrived from Snezhnaya. Rotwang sought to use the ideal heir of the Frostmoon Scions to reach the pitch-black Elysium beyond the heavens, which he had once glimpsed. But after the death of the blessed lady, who ended her own life when Rotwang's men tried to capture her, Lovia offered Rotwang the use of a sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions. At that time, a man named Solovei arrived in Nod-Krai and began to interfere with Lovia and Rotwang's plans. When Solovei met the twins, the elder sister posed as his close friend to gain his trust and went with him. Aila, the younger sister, was ordered by Lovia to kill Solovei, but she disobeyed, seeing him as the hero meant to protect Elysium. Over the long years of the girl's obedience, Lovia came to believe that suffering never once stirred resentment in her. So when the blessed Aila, destined to bear a sacred heir, pierced Lovia with a blade of pure silver, she could not comprehend the source of the betrayal.
After Alia sacrificed herself to stop Rotwang, a horrifying malice and hatred settled in Aila's soul. She didn't want to hurt Solovei's kind heart and couldn't tell him of her suffering, so she decided to cast aside everything that remained of the Archpriestess in order to save the children, who were pure and untainted by corruption. Everything born of the Frost Moon would return to it, all the temples destroyed, and then there would be no new Lovia or new Aila, tainted by sin.

Due to the purification of her blood, Aila foresaw that decades later, a new moon goddess would be born, and everything Lovia had so long and desperately sought would be in vain. She didn't know if she would live to see that day, as she couldn't see her own threads of fate, but she prayed that it wouldn't happen, for sinners are unworthy of seeing the pure light of the moon. But to prepare the Frostmoon Scions, she had to convince people that the new moon would delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid. Otherwise, no matter how noble the ideal, it would only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon. The new moon goddess was not obligated to give anything in return to her followers, and was not obligated to be the ideal deity for everyone. Aila became the first Moonchanter, rewrote the old prayers, hymns, and doctrines of the Frostmoon Scions, and consigned the name of Lovia to oblivion. The chamber where the Archpriestess's works were preserved was sealed, lest future descendants of the Frostmoon Scions bear the burden of her sins. And although Aila considered herself a sinner, unworthy of witnessing the birth of a new moon goddess, she witnessed her birth, gave her a drop of her blood on a blade of pure silver, and personally carved a statue on Hiisi Island.

customize.text: Heroes Meant to Protect "Elysium"

Even after Aila's older sister managed to seal Rotwang, Aila foresaw his return. <color=#ffffffd9>"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down... And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."</color> To combat Rotwang and the Abyssal forces that invaded Nod-Krai, the Moonchanter shared with Solovei a sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions left by Hyperborea, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. It was capable of transforming the energy of the Light Realm and purifying the energy of the
Borrowing the priestess's power, Solovei raised that first beam of light and, in the name of the moon, banished the darkness to those lightless ruins, burying it deep down alongside the nightmare-torn souls. As Aila had foretold, Rotwang returned as a being woven from the Abyss. Aila and Solovei were able to push the fiend and his followers back to Kipumaki Cliff and seal them there. To meet the future threat, Solovei founded the order of Lightkeepers in honor of the flame Aila had ignited. The Arrow of Terpikeraunas became the foundation for the Piramida lighthouse, illuminating the way in the darkness.
Despite her friendship with Solovei, she did not attend his funeral. When their mutual acquaintance went to see her on Hiisi Island, believing the priestess might not have known about the ceremony, he was met by a servant who timidly told him that Lady Moonchanter had long known of his arrival and what had happened to the Torchforger, but she did not wish to see him and asked him to return.

As Aila knew the seal placed on Rotwang would one day weaken and he would return to the world for a third time, she inscribed her image to leave a message for the hero of the sublunary sphere, who would rid the world of the undying serpent. Five hundred years after Rotwang's second death, the Traveler arrived in Nod-Krai, whom the priestess recognized as the hero meant to protect Elysium. Aila guided them and the priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, using the Ancient Moon Remnants, whose fall she had also foreseen, to remove the seal from the Court of the First Edict. She left them the last sword forged in moonlight by the Apostle of the Far North. It was with this blade Aila slew the Archpriestess Lovia, and with it she offered the first drop of silver blood to the newborn moon goddess.

desc.text:
...I told a lie, just like Lovia did, and just like my sister did. I said no when Mr. Solovei asked me if I felt any hate.
...But how can I put the hatred in my heart into words? How would someone as kind and sincere as he is ever understand such horrifying malice?
...No. I cannot think this way, and no one needs to know. Mr. Solovei does not need to be troubled with such trivial things. No one is obliged to bear the weight of another's suffering, which they have not experienced. And even if he truly were willing to listen, and even if his kindness were to move him to tears... what would it change? I would only end up bringing needless pain to another tender heart. In the past, the present, and the future, across the countless threads of fate that Lovia once let me glimpse by mistake, the only ones who shed tears for the misfortunes of others are kind souls who ought to be smiling instead. And since the sublunary sphere has always been one where good is repaid with cruelty, the least I could do is spare him a sorrow that does him no good.
...Once upon a time, I despised lies. Yet now, I find myself speaking them with keen intent. Maybe the [...] of the past dozen years or so has been punishment for this very moment...
...But that does not matter anymore. From the noble lady of Salt to the scions of Gurabad's jinni, there have been plenty of instances where the innocent have suffered the gravest of punishments, let alone a sinner as steeped in [...] as I am. If the silvery-white thread has already found its way around my neck, I may as well bear the weight of still more unforgivable sins by myself so that the children who remain untainted may be spared...
...What was born of the Frost Moon must return to it. All the walls, towers, fortresses, and temples must be torn down, save for the great pillar raised here by the Dragonborn, that is, the sacred sanctuary where our ancestors found refuge. Prolonged isolation and seclusion serve only to nourish fleeting ambitions and hollow delusions. Let it be reverence for nature, kindness toward outlanders, and those virtues in which none believe, and not the pride of the dead, which sets our threads apart from theirs. Only then will there never again be another Lovia... or another me.
...Decades from now, a new moon goddess will be born... Oh, the irony of it! Lovia's long and desperate quest was, in the end, for nothing. Even if [...] had borne the sacred heir as foretold, and not the man who abducted my sister... The one who should have been our sovereign would only have created even greater chaos in Snezhnaya. The birth of the new moon had nothing to do with anything she did. She could not even foresee the coming of that maiden, and nor did she know that the holy throne had never truly been broken...
...I do not know if I will live to see that moment, for my own thread is hidden from my sight. But I pray that I will not. Those tainted by sin do not deserve to witness the moon's pure light...
...In any case, people must come to believe that the new moon takes delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid — that no other prayer or sacrifice will ever please our goddess. This is what they must believe, because if they do not, then no matter how noble the ideal, it will only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon...
...The threads of the gods are too bright for me to follow, and I cannot see where she is headed. But at the very least, the Frostmoon Scions, who have been redeemed in her name, must ensure that the power of choice remains hers alone. No one should ever seek repayment or reward from her, and she must never be molded into the "perfect deity" others wish her to become...
...Daughter of the Frost Moon, maiden of the new moon... May she one day behold the dream of true happiness... and may the Frost Moon never forgive my sins, for I have cursed her name more times than I can count.

Dear Miss Aila,
I am truly sorry that I was unable to stop Miss Alia in that moment. Yet, it was through her noble sacrifice that we ultimately thwarted Rotwang and prevented the loss of countless lives. Now, I finally understand why she pretended to be my close companion. I hope to speak with you about this in greater detail when next we meet — though perhaps, by then, you will already know more about all this than I.
I shall not presume to judge, nor shall I attempt to alter your opinion of her. But I ask, if nothing else, that you allow me to honor Miss Alia's final wishes by sharing her words with you. She asked that I render all possible support to you (which I surely will. You are my benefactor, after all), and that — I relay this only as she spoke it — she hoped that you would go on to live a life of happiness and freedom.
As for the Arrow of Terpikeraunas you mentioned in your last letter, if it truly holds the power to dispel the pitch-black calamity, and if you are willing to share it with such selflessness, then on behalf of the people of Nod-Krai, please accept my deepest gratitude. Should, as you foresee, Rotwang indeed rise again from the pitch-black filth, then our successors — an order I am considering naming the "Lightkeepers," in honor of the flame you have kindled — will stand ready to vanquish the threat once more, armed with the technology you have so generously gifted us.
We can speak of the details in person whenever you are free. I understand all too well that, after Lovia's passing, the Frostmoon Scions have been left with countless matters demanding your attention.
Yours sincerely,
Solovei
